page.title: From Golf Swings to Scalable Motion Analysis
page.description: An RGB-camera proof of concept for making movement analysis more accessible, starting with golf.
page.role: A focused golf proof of concept. A repeatable path toward accessible motion analysis.
page.footer: Golf swing analysis · Proof of concept

sections.title: Executive Summary
paragraphs: Reliable movement analysis can help people improve performance, support rehabilitation, and understand how the body moves. Specialized capture equipment, controlled spaces, and expert setup can make it difficult to deliver broadly. This project explores a more accessible approach: extracting useful motion information from RGB video, starting with golf as a focused proof of concept.
Four connected projects improve body tracking, integrate golfer and club detection, recover blurred clubs, and stabilize trajectories—building a reusable foundation for video-based analysis.

sections.title: Business Opportunity
paragraphs: Motion analysis creates value when it turns movement into information someone can use: a coach identifying a swing issue, a practitioner monitoring exercise, or an operator reviewing a physical task.

Marker-based capture can involve dedicated cameras, calibration, space, careful marker placement, and manual cleanup. Clothing and attachment requirements can add friction for the person being recorded. These demands make routine use and expansion across locations difficult.

The opportunity is to reduce the equipment and expertise needed to obtain useful movement information. RGB video offers a practical route toward more accessible services built around the requirements of each application.

sections.title: Golf as a Proof of Concept
paragraphs: Golf combines a focused capture setup with demanding motion. Common face-on and down-the-line views constrain the recording conditions, and a single golfer lets the initial work concentrate on detection. Existing coaching practices provide a vocabulary for interpreting movement.

Body rotation, unusual poses, occlusion, and rapid club motion still create difficult visual problems. Solving these within a defined workflow makes golf a useful proof of concept and establishes a development pattern to apply elsewhere.

sections.title: Technical Approach
paragraphs: Useful feedback starts with dependable movement information. These projects address successive points where raw footage can lose that information.

projects.title: Improving Golf Swing Pose Estimation
projects.summary: Body rotation and unusual swing positions challenge general-purpose pose models. Golf-specific improvements strengthen the body tracking that downstream analysis depends on.

projects.title: Integrating Golfer and Club Detection
projects.summary: Separate detections leave an incomplete picture of the swing. Bringing body and club information into one pipeline makes their movement easier to interpret together.

projects.title: Enhancing Blurry Club Recall
projects.summary: Fast club motion can blur the club head and cause missed detections. Targeted improvements recover more of this difficult motion for subsequent analysis.

projects.title: Trajectory Postprocessing
projects.summary: Frame-by-frame predictions can produce jittery motion traces. Sequence-based reconstruction reduces instability while preserving the sharp movement around impact.

sections.title: Results
paragraphs: Explore body and club tracking in a single view. Play a swing or step through individual frames; select joints to inspect their motion trails.

sections.title: Expansion Strategy
paragraphs: The repeatable pattern is to choose a valuable movement, define the capture conditions, improve detection, and turn the resulting information into a domain-specific service. Other sports, exercise and rehabilitation monitoring, workplace ergonomics, animation, and human–robot interaction offer potential applications. Each has its own capture and precision requirements.

subsections.title: Business models
paragraphs: A consumer subscription could support recurring swing review. Tools for coaches, academies, and simulator operators could support more efficient analysis and progress tracking. Partners could embed the experience in their own services through a B2B2C offering, while an API or SDK could make the perception pipeline available to other products.

subsections.title: The next step
paragraphs: A focused pilot with coaches or training facilities would connect the technology to repeat usage and expert feedback. The commercial priorities are a simple recording process, understandable output, less review effort, and a service customers find useful enough to return to.

sections.title: Conclusion
paragraphs: Golf is the first application of a broader idea: making useful motion analysis accessible through RGB video. The four projects tackle the perception and trajectory problems between raw footage and usable movement information.
The business opportunity is a repeatable service model that reduces capture friction, delivers value within a focused workflow, and expands into other movement-based applications.
